leverage.exposure: The balance is negative and must be back above zero before the matchday locks on 09.10 at 18:30Z, or the entire matchday scores nothing. That is the one risk that outranks everything else here. It is not yet urgent - the lock is more than four days out and the Treu sale alone covers the deficit with room to spare - but the action that delivers it has a much earlier deadline than the lock does, because the listing has to be pulled before the 06.10 tick. If both flips win, the deficit deepens temporarily; that is expected and self-correcting, since each flip is unwound by selling the same player back to Kickbase after the tick, and the combined unwind of Treu plus both flips clears the balance comfortably. The discipline is that every flip must be unwound to a non-negative balance and at least eleven players before the lock, and no flip may reduce the fielded eleven - neither of tonight's candidates does, since one is a reserve goalkeeper and the other a third striker. Note for the record that the notification rule that fires on an open leveraged position still has no lock-proximity scope, so it will keep firing on every run until the balance clears; that defect is already on file.

binding_gap: There is no formation hole to fix, which is why no buy leads the briefing. The eleven is filled and three formations remain legal. The gap that does bind is positional depth rather than count: with Ruoppi gone the squad can no longer field any five-midfielder shape, and the sole bench player is a defender, so the midfield and attack have no cover at all. Selling Treu as planned takes the squad to the bare minimum, where the only legal shape is the one currently being fielded and every remaining player is load-bearing. That is acceptable before the lock because the sale is what clears the balance, and a cleared balance is worth more than bench depth. But it means no further sale can be made after Treu without a replacement landing first, and it means a late dropout in midfield or attack before the lock would have no answer.

verdict.detail: Both standing sell instructions have now been carried out or overtaken, and the run turns up no new buy worth making. Ruoppi was sold back to Kickbase at market value, exactly as SELL Su8gfgw asked, and the proceeds have shrunk the deficit without touching the fielded eleven. What remains is one time-bound housekeeping action on the primary unwind leg: the standing manager ask on Treu has to come off the market before the 06.10 20:00Z tick, because from that tick onward his own market value overtakes the price it is listed at and the ask turns into a gift for whichever rival notices first. Pull the listing, then sell him back to Kickbase after the 08.10 tick and before the lock. That single change is worth more than every flip on the board combined, and it is the action that clears the balance. Nothing else on the market clears the points bar, so nothing else is recommended.

sell.reason: Treu is the only sale on the books and it stays on the books, unchanged in substance from S9cv1ds. He is confirmed fit: ligainsider's profile carries a green fit marker, Kickbase shows no status flag, and his most recent dated item, from 04.09.2026, concerns a selection contest with Kuebler for the right-back slot rather than any injury. The sale is therefore a balance decision, not a fitness decision. The sequencing matters more than the decision: hold him through the 08.10 tick, because he is trending upward and four daily ticks at the measured rising-flag drift take him comfortably past the price his own listing is asking. But the listing itself must come off first. It has sat unsold for more than three days without drawing a single offer, so the chance of it clearing at the asking price is slight, while the chance of it becoming a below-market giveaway after the 06.10 tick is near certain. Pull it, wait for the tick, sell back to Kickbase.

One tick takes mv to about 13.222.600, still under the ask; two ticks take it to about 13.554.500, ABOVE the ask. From that moment Georg is offering his own best unwind asset below market, and kb_context's own standing measurement is that sub-mv manager asks do not survive — 'manager asks below mv right now: 0' has held every run. THE CALL: remove_offer on Treu no later than 2026-10-06T20:00:00Z, then sell_player to Kickbase at exactly mv after the 2026-10-08T20:00Z tick and before the lock. Selling to Kickbase pays exactly mv with no spread, measured 8 for 8. FIELDED COST, stated honestly: Treu is fielded at ap 76 and Nakuzola (ap 27) replaces him, so the XI falls 1353 -> 1304, -49 for MD5. That cost is unavoidable — the deficit must be cleared — and it is the reason the Ruoppi leg (Su8gfgw, points-free off the bench) must go first.

buy.reason: No buy is recommended, and this is a finding rather than an omission. The board was swept in full and nothing on it improves the eleven. The buyable Kickbase listings are all either well below the average of the weakest player they would displace, or carry a falling-value flag, or are the familiar trap of a flattering season average built on a handful of cameo minutes - Konstantelias is the clearest example of the latter and stays on the avoid list. Every manager ask on the board is priced above market value, and a manager ask above market value has never once been a buy in this ledger's history; the whole JakobDohr batch, El Aynaoui, Querfeld, Neuhaus, Tigges and the rest remain avoided on exactly that ground. Spending power is ample and that is not the constraint - the constraint is that there is nothing worth spending it on. Padding the list with a defender who would not displace anyone would cost points, not gain them.

movers.reason: The flip mechanism is intact and the re-measurement shows no decay in the rising-flag edge - the sample has grown again and both the mean next-tick move and the share of listings that rose are unchanged from the last reading, so no crowding is yet visible. Two listings qualify for tonight's tick and both are already open calls: Zentner, the larger and better of the two, and Rondic, which is marginal but costless. Both are Kickbase board listings with the price set exactly at market value and a rising flag, and both expire before tonight's update, which is what puts them inside the capture window. Bid exactly market value on each and never raise - Bensebaini, the third candidate from the last sweep, was lost this morning to a rival who paid far into the high contested band, and that is the outcome the no-raise rule exists to avoid. Losing an auction at market value costs nothing; winning one at that kind of premium wipes out a long run of good flips. Zentner is flagged as carrying a knock and Rondic surfaces a loud loan story, but neither blocks the trade: fitness does not enter the market-value tick, and the loan cluster is dated to the summer 2025 window, with the next transfer window not opening until January. Two other listings, Capaldo and the newly listed Soylu, have the right shape but expire too late to catch tonight's tick, so they are logged as watches rather than bids - a rising flag predicts the next update only, and by the time those clear it will have been re-rolled. The two open questions stand: it is still unknown whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can run at once, and the edge remains measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals crowd in.

A sky.de headline saying Treu is out until further notice is dated 04.08.2025 and describes a shoulder injury from a pre-season friendly two seasons ago; it is the second such trap on Treu after the February item already on file. Rondic's loan-away story is dated 11.08.2025. Assume any undated hit is stale - that rule earned its keep twice today.
